packages.name: com.landawn.abacus.annotation
packages.summary: Annotations for API contracts, entity mapping, JSON/XML serialization, mutability, nullability, and stream-pipeline characteristics.

types.name: AccessFieldByMethod
types.javadoc_summary: Forces property access on a bean to go through getter / setter methods rather than direct field reflection.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: String value() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Reserved for future configuration use; currently has no effect on the framework's behavior.
methods.returns: the (currently unused) configuration value; defaults to an empty string
examples:
@AccessFieldByMethod              // uses the default empty value; equivalent to @AccessFieldByMethod("").
public class User { }

types.name: Beta
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated API element is in beta stage and subject to change or removal in future versions.

types.name: Column
types.javadoc_summary: Specifies that a field represents a database column in an entity class.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: @Deprecated String value() default ""

deprecated.message: Use #name() to specify the column name explicitly.

methods.javadoc_summary: Deprecated alias for #name().
methods.returns: the column name, or an empty string if not specified
contract: When both are specified, this element wins: #name() is consulted only if this one is empty.

methods.name: name
methods.signature: String name() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: The name of the database column this field maps to.
methods.returns: the column name, or an empty string to use the field name as default
contract: If not specified (empty string), the field name is used as the column name.
examples:
@Column(name = "created_date")
private LocalDateTime createdDate;

types.name: DiffIgnore
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that a field should be excluded from bean difference comparison operations.

types.name: Entity
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a class as a persistent entity that maps to a database table.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: @Deprecated String value() default ""

deprecated.message: Use #name() to specify the entity name explicitly.

methods.javadoc_summary: Deprecated alias for #name().
methods.returns: the entity name, or an empty string if not specified

methods.name: name
methods.signature: String name() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: The name of the entity, which typically maps to the database table name.
methods.returns: the entity name, or empty string to use the simple class name as default
contract: If not specified (empty string), the simple class name is used as the entity name.

types.name: Id
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a field or type as representing the primary key (identifier) of an entity.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: String[] value() default {}
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the property names that form the primary key when `@Id` is applied to a type (class) to declare a composite or explicit primary key.
methods.returns: the property names forming the primary key at the type level; an empty array (the default) is the conventional value for field-level usage
contract: Usage patterns: For type-level usage: list one or more property names that form the primary key (the array must be non-empty at the type level).
For field-level usage: this element is typically left at its default (empty array); the annotated field itself identifies the primary key, and any column-name mapping should be supplied via Column.

types.name: Immutable
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated type is immutable or that the annotated method returns an immutable value.

types.name: IntermediateOp
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a method as an intermediate operation in stream-like or pipeline processing.

types.name: Internal
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated element is for internal use only and should not be used by external code or client applications.

types.name: JoinedBy
types.javadoc_summary: Declares a join relationship between entities for ORM mapping and lazy / eager loading of related data.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: String[] value() default {}
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the join conditions that define how entities are related.
methods.returns: an array of join condition strings defining the relationship

types.name: JsonXmlConfig
types.javadoc_summary: Configures JSON and XML serialization/deserialization behavior for the annotated class.

methods.name: namingPolicy
methods.signature: NamingPolicy namingPolicy() default NamingPolicy.CAMEL_CASE
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the naming policy to use when converting field names during serialization.
methods.returns: the naming policy to apply to field names during serialization

methods.name: ignoredFields
methods.signature: String[] ignoredFields() default {}
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies fields to omit from serialized JSON/XML output.
methods.returns: an array of field names or regex patterns to exclude from serialization
contract: Serialization only: a matching property is still populated when input containing it is deserialized (and is not reported as an unknown property).
A matching field must keep JsonXmlField#direction() at its default; any other direction is rejected with an `IllegalArgumentException` when the bean is first introspected.

methods.name: dateFormat
methods.signature: String dateFormat() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the date format pattern to use when serializing and deserializing supported date/time fields.
methods.returns: the date format pattern, or an empty string for no class-level pattern override
contract: When Joda-Time is present, `DateTime` and `MutableDateTime` fields use its `DateTimeFormat` syntax.

methods.name: timeZone
methods.signature: String timeZone() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the time zone to use for date/time serialization.
methods.returns: the time zone ID, or an empty string for the system default time zone
contract: If empty, the system default time zone is used.
The ID is trimmed and resolved with java.util.TimeZone#getTimeZone(String) when the bean is first introspected.

An unrecognised ID (a typo such as `"America/New York"` or `"UTC+1"`) is not rejected - it silently resolves to GMT, shifting every formatted instant without an error; custom offsets must use the form `"GMT+02:00"`.

methods.name: numberFormat
methods.signature: String numberFormat() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the number format pattern to use for numeric values during serialization.
methods.returns: the number format pattern, or an empty string for default representation
contract: If empty, numbers are serialized using their default string representation.

methods.name: enumerated
methods.signature: EnumType enumerated() default EnumType.NAME
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies how enum values are serialized and deserialized.
methods.returns: the enum serialization strategy

methods.name: exclusion
methods.signature: Exclusion exclusion() default Exclusion.NULL
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the exclusion policy for field serialization.
methods.returns: the exclusion policy to apply during serialization
contract: Determines which fields should be excluded from the serialized output.

types.name: JsonXmlCreator
types.javadoc_summary: Designates the static factory method that should be invoked when an object is reconstructed from a single serialized value (JSON, XML, or persistence).

types.name: JsonXmlField
types.javadoc_summary: Configures JSON and XML serialization/deserialization behavior for individual fields.

methods.name: name
methods.signature: String name() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the field name to use in JSON/XML serialization.
methods.returns: the field name for serialization, or an empty string for the default Java field name
contract: If not specified (empty string), the Java field name is used.
examples:
@JsonXmlField(name = "user_id")
private Long id;  // maps to "user_id" instead of "id"

methods.name: aliases
methods.signature: String[] aliases() default {}
methods.javadoc_summary: Defines alternative names that can be used during deserialization.
methods.returns: an array of alias names for deserialization

methods.name: type
methods.signature: String type() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the explicit type for field serialization/deserialization.
methods.returns: the explicit type string, or an empty string for automatic type detection
examples:
@JsonXmlField(type = "java.util.Date")
private Object dateValue;  // treats value as Date type

methods.name: dateFormat
methods.signature: String dateFormat() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the date format pattern for date/time field serialization and deserialization.
methods.returns: the date format pattern, or an empty string for the default format
contract: When Joda-Time is present, `DateTime` and `MutableDateTime` fields use its `DateTimeFormat` syntax.
Formatted text uses normal string escaping when JSON string quotation is enabled, including literal quotation marks, backslashes and control characters in the pattern.

methods.name: timeZone
methods.signature: String timeZone() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the time zone for date/time field serialization.
methods.returns: the time zone ID (e.g., `"UTC"`, `"America/New_York"`), or an empty string for the system default
contract: The ID is trimmed and resolved with java.util.TimeZone#getTimeZone(String) when the bean is first introspected.

methods.name: numberFormat
methods.signature: String numberFormat() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the number format pattern for numeric field serialization.
methods.returns: the number format pattern, or an empty string for default formatting

methods.name: enumerated
methods.signature: EnumType enumerated() default EnumType.NAME
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies how enum values are serialized and deserialized for this field.
methods.returns: the enum serialization strategy
examples:
@JsonXmlField(enumerated = EnumType.ORDINAL)
private Status status;  // 0, 1, 2... instead of "ACTIVE", "INACTIVE"...

methods.name: ignore
methods.signature: boolean ignore() default false
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies whether this field is omitted from serialized JSON/XML output.
methods.returns: `true` to omit this field from serialized output, `false` to include it
contract: When set to `true`, the property is never written by the JSON/XML serializers.

To write a property but never read it, use #direction() `= Direction.SERIALIZE_ONLY` instead; combining `ignore = true` with a non-default #direction() is rejected with an `IllegalArgumentException` when the bean is first introspected.

methods.name: isJsonRawValue
methods.signature: boolean isJsonRawValue() default false
methods.javadoc_summary: Indicates whether the field value should be written as a JSON payload.
methods.returns: `true` to write a JSON payload, `false` for normal processing
contract: In JSON output, a character-sequence value is inserted directly without additional quoting or escaping; it must already contain valid JSON.

methods.name: direction
methods.signature: Direction direction() default Direction.BOTH
methods.javadoc_summary: Controls whether the field is included during serialization, deserialization, or both.
methods.returns: the exposure mode for this field
contract: Options: Direction#BOTH - Include in both serialization and deserialization (default) Direction#SERIALIZE_ONLY - Include only when writing JSON/XML output Direction#DESERIALIZE_ONLY - Include only when reading from JSON/XML input Usage Examples:

types.name: Direction
types.javadoc_summary: Defines the exposure levels for field serialization and deserialization operations.

fields.name: BOTH
fields.javadoc_summary: The field participates in both serialization and deserialization operations.

fields.name: SERIALIZE_ONLY
fields.javadoc_summary: The field is only included during serialization (object to JSON/XML).

fields.name: DESERIALIZE_ONLY
fields.javadoc_summary: The field is only included during deserialization (JSON/XML to object).

types.name: JsonXmlValue
types.javadoc_summary: Marks the single property whose value represents the entire object when serialized.

types.name: LazyEvaluation
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated method or type uses a lazy evaluation strategy.

types.name: MayReturnNull
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated method may return `null` values under certain conditions.

types.name: Mutable
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated type has mutable state or that the annotated method mutates state.

types.name: NonColumn
types.javadoc_summary: Explicitly marks a field as NOT mapping to a database column.

types.name: NonUpdatable
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a field as non-updatable, excluding it from `UPDATE` operations while allowing `INSERT`s.

types.name: NotNull
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated element must not be `null`.

types.name: NullSafe
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated element gracefully handles `null` values without throwing exceptions.

types.name: ParallelSupported
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated method or type supports parallel execution within an abacus pipeline.

types.name: ReadOnly
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a field as read-only for database persistence operations.

types.name: ReadOnlyId
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a field (or names properties at the type level) as a read-only identifier — a primary key that is managed by the database and must not be written by the application.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: String[] value() default {}
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the property names that form the read-only primary key when `@ReadOnlyId` is applied to a type (class).
methods.returns: the property names forming the read-only identifier at the type level; an empty array (the default) is the conventional value for field-level usage
contract: Usage patterns: For type-level usage: list one or more property names that comprise the read-only primary key (the array must be non-empty at the type level).

types.name: Record
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a class as a record-like entity, telling abacus introspection to treat it as if it were a Java 14+ java.lang.Record even when it does not extend java.lang.Record (for example, a Lombok `@Value` class compiled under Java 8 source level).

types.name: SequentialOnly
types.javadoc_summary: Indicates that the annotated method or type must run sequentially and is NOT safe to use on a parallelized abacus pipeline.

types.name: Stateful
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a class, method, or field as stateful, indicating that behavior depends on state that can change between invocations or over time.

types.name: SuppressFBWarnings
types.javadoc_summary: Annotation used to suppress FindBugs/SpotBugs warnings on annotated program elements.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: String[] value() default {}
methods.javadoc_summary: The set of FindBugs warnings that are to be suppressed in an annotated element.
methods.returns: an array of FindBugs warning identifiers to suppress

methods.name: justification
methods.signature: String justification() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Optional documentation of the reason why the warning is suppressed.
methods.returns: the justification for suppressing the warning, or an empty string if not provided
contract: This field should provide a clear explanation of why suppressing the warning is appropriate.
Note if the issue is addressed elsewhere in the codebase.

types.name: Table
types.javadoc_summary: Specifies that the annotated class is mapped to a database table.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: @Deprecated String value() default ""

deprecated.message: Use #name() to specify the table name explicitly.

methods.javadoc_summary: Deprecated alias for #name().
methods.returns: the table name, or an empty string if not specified
contract: When both are specified, this element wins: #name() is consulted only if this one is empty.

methods.name: name
methods.signature: String name() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: The name of the database table this class maps to.
methods.returns: the table name, or an empty string to use the simple class name as default
contract: If not specified (empty string), the simple class name is used as the table name.
examples:
@Table(name = "user_accounts")  // maps to 'user_accounts' table
public class User { }

methods.name: alias
methods.signature: String alias() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: An alias for the table that can be used in SQL queries.
methods.returns: the table alias, or an empty string if no alias is defined
contract: This provides a shorter reference name for the table, useful in complex queries with joins, subqueries, or when the table name is long.

methods.name: columnFields
methods.signature: String[] columnFields() default {}
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies an explicit whitelist of fields for mapping consumers that support table-field metadata.
methods.returns: an array of field names to include as columns for supporting consumers, an empty array means no whitelist metadata
contract: When applied by a consumer, only these fields should be considered for column mapping.

methods.name: nonColumnFields
methods.signature: String[] nonColumnFields() default {}
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies a blacklist of fields for mapping consumers that support table-field metadata.
methods.returns: an array of field names to exclude from column mapping for supporting consumers, an empty array means no blacklist metadata
contract: These fields should be excluded from column mapping by supporting consumers, useful for transient data, calculated fields, or framework-specific properties.
Usage Examples: Note: If both `columnFields` and `nonColumnFields` are specified, supporting consumers should let `columnFields` take precedence (whitelist wins over blacklist).

types.name: TerminalOp
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a method as a terminal operation in stream-like or pipeline processing.

types.name: TerminalOpTriggered
types.javadoc_summary: Marks intermediate operations that perform terminal-style materialization of their upstream before the returned stream can produce elements.

types.name: Test
types.javadoc_summary: Marks elements that are intended for testing purposes only and should not be used in production code.

types.name: Transient
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a field as transient — i.e., excluded from persistence operations.

types.name: Type
types.javadoc_summary: Specifies custom type handling for fields or methods during serialization and persistence operations.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: @Deprecated String value() default ""

deprecated.message: Use #name() to specify the type name explicitly.

methods.javadoc_summary: Deprecated alias for #name().
methods.returns: the type name, or an empty string if not specified
contract: When both are specified, this element wins: #name() is consulted only if this one is empty.

methods.name: name
methods.signature: String name() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the type name to use for type conversion.
methods.returns: the type name, or empty string to use default type handling
contract: This should match a registered type name in the `TypeFactory`.

methods.name: clazz
methods.signature: @SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") Class<? extends com.landawn.abacus.type.Type> clazz() default com.landawn.abacus.type.Type.class
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies a custom `Type` class to handle value conversion.
methods.returns: the custom Type implementation class to use, or Type.class itself when no custom type handling is needed
contract: The specified class must implement com.landawn.abacus.type.Type (typically by extending com.landawn.abacus.type.AbstractType) and provide the necessary conversion methods.
The custom type class should: Have a no-argument constructor; or, when #name() (or deprecated #value()) is specified, a constructor accepting one String.
The single-argument constructor is preferred when both are present.
Override the necessary conversion methods Be thread-safe if used in concurrent contexts Usage Examples:

methods.name: enumerated
methods.signature: EnumType enumerated() default EnumType.NAME
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies how enum values should be represented during conversion.
methods.returns: the enum representation strategy, defaults to EnumType#NAME
contract: Precedence for JSON/XML: when the field also carries @JsonXmlField, or its class carries @JsonXmlConfig, the JSON/XML serializers take the enum representation from those annotations (see JsonXmlField#enumerated()) and this element is not consulted for JSON/XML output - a class-level `@JsonXmlConfig(enumerated = ORDINAL)` wins over `@Type(enumerated = NAME)`.

Within its #scope(), this element governs the property's general and database conversions: `PropInfo.type` when the scope is Scope#ALL or Scope#SERIALIZATION, and `PropInfo.dbType` when it is Scope#ALL or Scope#PERSISTENCE.

EnumType#NAME (default): Uses the enum constant name as a string More readable and maintainable Resilient to enum reordering Larger storage size EnumType#ORDINAL: Uses the enum ordinal position as an integer Smaller storage size Fragile - breaks if enum order changes Less readable in raw data EnumType#CODE: Uses a predefined integer code from the enum (for example, via `public int code()`) Compact representation with stable code values Requires the enum to expose consistent code values Usage Examples:

methods.name: scope
methods.signature: Scope scope() default Scope.ALL
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the scope where this type conversion should apply.
methods.returns: the scope of type conversion, defaults to Scope#ALL

types.name: Scope
types.javadoc_summary: Defines the operational contexts where custom type conversion should be applied.

fields.name: SERIALIZATION
fields.javadoc_summary: Apply type conversion for serialization/deserialization operations.

fields.name: PERSISTENCE
fields.javadoc_summary: Apply type conversion for database persistence operations.

fields.name: ALL
fields.javadoc_summary: Apply type conversion in all contexts (both serialization and persistence).

types.name: UnsupportedOperation
types.javadoc_summary: Marks methods that represent unsupported operations in an implementation.

packages.name: com.landawn.abacus.exception
packages.summary: Runtime exceptions used by Abacus APIs.

types.name: DuplicateResultException
types.javadoc_summary: Exception thrown when an operation that expects a unique result encounters duplicate results.

constructors.signature: public DuplicateResultException()
constructors.javadoc_summary: Constructs a new `DuplicateResultException` with no detail message.
examples: throw new DuplicateResultException();

constructors.signature: public DuplicateResultException(final String message)
constructors.javadoc_summary: Constructs a new `DuplicateResultException` with the specified detail message.

params.name: message
params.javadoc: the detail message. The detail message is saved for later retrieval by the #getMessage() method.

examples: throw new DuplicateResultException("Found multiple records for unique ID: " + id);

constructors.signature: public DuplicateResultException(final String message, final Throwable cause)
constructors.javadoc_summary: Constructs a new `DuplicateResultException` with the specified detail message and cause.

params.name: message
params.javadoc: the detail message. The detail message is saved for later retrieval by the #getMessage() method.

params.name: cause
params.javadoc: the cause (which is saved for later retrieval by the #getCause() method). (A `null` value is permitted, and indicates that the cause is nonexistent or unknown.)

constructors.signature: public DuplicateResultException(final Throwable cause)
constructors.javadoc_summary: Constructs a new `DuplicateResultException` with the specified cause and a detail message of `(cause == null? null: cause.toString())` (which typically contains the class and detail message of `cause`).

params.name: cause
params.javadoc: the cause (which is saved for later retrieval by the #getCause() method). (A `null` value is permitted, and indicates that the cause is nonexistent or unknown.)

types.name: HttpResponseException
types.javadoc_summary: Thrown when an HTTP request completes with a non-successful status code and the caller did not ask for the raw HttpResponse.

constructors.signature: public HttpResponseException(final String requestUrl, final int statusCode, final String responseMessage, final Map<String, List<String>> headers, final String responseBody, final byte[] rawResponseBody, final Throwable decodingFailure)
constructors.javadoc_summary: Creates an HTTP failure retaining an undecodable error body's raw prefix and its decoding failure.

params.name: requestUrl
params.javadoc: request URL, or null when unavailable

params.name: statusCode
params.javadoc: HTTP status

params.name: responseMessage
params.javadoc: reason phrase, or null

params.name: headers
params.javadoc: response headers, copied

params.name: responseBody
params.javadoc: best-effort text, or null

params.name: rawResponseBody
params.javadoc: raw bytes, or null when unavailable

params.name: decodingFailure
params.javadoc: failure while decoding the body, or null

constructors.signature: public HttpResponseException(final String requestUrl, final int statusCode, final String responseMessage, final Map<String, List<String>> headers, final String responseBody)
constructors.javadoc_summary: Creates a new `HttpResponseException`.

params.name: requestUrl
params.javadoc: the URL the failing request was sent to; may be `null`

params.name: statusCode
params.javadoc: the HTTP status code of the response

params.name: responseMessage
params.javadoc: the HTTP status message of the response; may be `null` or empty, in which case it is omitted from the message

params.name: headers
params.javadoc: the response headers, copied along with their value lists; may be `null`, in which case an empty map is used. Null keys, lists and list elements are preserved.

params.name: responseBody
params.javadoc: the captured (possibly truncated) error body; may be `null`, in which case an empty string is used

methods.name: rawResponseBody
methods.signature: public byte[] rawResponseBody()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the raw error-body prefix captured before decoding failed.
methods.returns: a defensive copy of at most HttpUtil#MAX_ERROR_BODY_SIZE bytes, or `null` when unavailable

methods.name: responseBodyDecodingFailure
methods.signature: public Throwable responseBodyDecodingFailure()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the original failure encountered while decoding the error body.
methods.returns: the body decoding failure, or `null` when none was recorded

methods.name: statusCode
methods.signature: public int statusCode()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the HTTP status code of the response.
methods.returns: the HTTP status code, for example `404`

methods.name: responseMessage
methods.signature: public String responseMessage()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the HTTP status message of the response.
methods.returns: the HTTP status message, for example `"Not Found"`; may be `null`

methods.name: requestUrl
methods.signature: public String requestUrl()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the URL the failing request was sent to.
methods.returns: the request URL, or `null` if it was not available

methods.name: headers
methods.signature: public Map<String, List<String>> headers()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the captured response headers, keyed as reported by the underlying connection.
methods.returns: an unmodifiable snapshot of the response headers; never `null`

methods.name: header
methods.signature: public String header(final String name)

params.name: name
params.javadoc: the header name to look up; `null` matches nothing and yields `null`

methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the first value of the named response header, matched case-insensitively.
methods.returns: the first value of the header, or `null` if the header is absent or has no value
contract: When the snapshot holds several keys that differ only in case, the first one in encounter order wins.

methods.name: headers
methods.signature: public List<String> headers(final String name)

params.name: name
params.javadoc: the header name to look up; `null` matches nothing and yields an empty list

methods.javadoc_summary: Returns all values of the named response header, matched case-insensitively.
methods.returns: an unmodifiable snapshot of the header values, or an empty list if the header is absent or its value list is `null`
contract: When the snapshot holds several keys that differ only in case, the first one in encounter order wins.

methods.name: responseBody
methods.signature: public String responseBody()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the captured error response body.
methods.returns: the captured error body; never `null`, empty when there was none
contract: The body is truncated to HttpUtil#MAX_ERROR_BODY_SIZE bytes when it is read, so this may be a prefix of the full response.

types.name: ObjectNotFoundException

constructors.signature: public ObjectNotFoundException(final String message)

constructors.signature: public ObjectNotFoundException(final Throwable cause)

types.name: ParsingException
types.javadoc_summary: Unchecked exception thrown when a parsing operation fails.

constructors.signature: public ParsingException()
constructors.javadoc_summary: Constructs a new `ParsingException` with no detail message.
examples: throw new ParsingException();

constructors.signature: public ParsingException(final String message)
constructors.javadoc_summary: Constructs a new `ParsingException` with the specified detail message.

params.name: message
params.javadoc: the detail message. The detail message is saved for later retrieval by the #getMessage() method.

examples: throw new ParsingException("Malformed JSON at line " + lineNumber);

constructors.signature: public ParsingException(final String message, final int errorToken)
constructors.javadoc_summary: Constructs a new `ParsingException` with the specified detail message and token.

params.name: message
params.javadoc: the detail message. The detail message is saved for later retrieval by the #getMessage() method.

params.name: errorToken
params.javadoc: an integer value representing the token, position, or error code where the parsing failed. This value can be retrieved later using #getErrorToken().

examples:

constructors.signature: public ParsingException(final String message, final int errorToken, final Throwable cause)
constructors.javadoc_summary: Constructs a new `ParsingException` with the specified detail message, token, and cause.

params.name: message

throws.condition: if the directory could not be created, such as if the system does not support creating temporary directories securely.

deprecated.message: For Android users, see the Data and File Storage overview to select an appropriate temporary directory (perhaps `context.getCacheDir()`), and create your own directory under that. (For example, you might use `new File(context.getCacheDir(), "directoryName").mkdir()`, or, if you need an arbitrary number of temporary directories, you might have to generate multiple directory names in a loop until `mkdir()` returns `true`.) For JRE users, prefer java.nio.file.Files#createTempDirectory, transforming it to a File using toFile() if needed. To restrict permissions as this method does, pass `PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute(PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rwx------"))` to your call to `createTempDirectory`.

methods.javadoc_summary: Atomically creates a new directory somewhere beneath the system's temporary directory (as defined by the `java.io.tmpdir` system property), and returns its name.
methods.returns: the newly created directory.
contract: If that is not possible (as is the case under the very old Android Ice Cream Sandwich release), then this method throws an exception instead of creating a directory that would be more accessible.

Previous versions would create a directory that is more accessible, as discussed in CVE-2020-8908.) Use this method instead of File#createTempFile(String, String) when you wish to create a directory, not a regular file.

A common pitfall is to call `createTempFile`, delete the file and create a directory in its place, but this leads a race condition which can be exploited to create security vulnerabilities, especially when executable files are to be written into the directory.

methods.javadoc_summary: Moves a file from one path to another.
contract: In either case `to` must be the target path for the file itself; not just the new name for the file or the path to the new parent directory.
If that fails, it falls back to copying the contents of `from` to `to` and then deleting `from`.

The copy+delete fallback runs whenever the rename fails: across volumes, when `from` is locked, and on Windows for every move onto an existing file (`File.renameTo` never replaces one there), even on the same volume.
If `from` cannot be deleted after the copy, `to` is deleted and an IOException is thrown: `from` survives, but the previously existing destination is gone.
Only ATOMIC_MOVE, which works only within one volume, keeps the destination intact when the move fails.

If `to` is another name of the existing regular file `from` (as determined by java.nio.file.Files#isSameFile(Path, Path)), only the rename is attempted, because the copy+delete fallback would truncate the file and then delete it.

A rename that succeeds (for example onto a `"./"` spelling of the same name) completes as usual; when it fails (for example onto a UNC or mapped-drive alias on Windows) an IllegalArgumentException is thrown and the file is left untouched.

methods.javadoc_summary: Creates a new traverser for a directed acyclic graph that has at most one path from the start node to any node reachable from the start node, such as a tree.

contract: This method is optimized for tree-like structures and will perform better than #forGraph(Function) when the graph is known to be a tree.

Providing graphs that don't conform to the tree structure may lead to: Traversal not terminating (if the graph has cycles) Nodes being visited multiple times (if multiple paths exist from the start node to any node reachable from it) In these cases, use #forGraph(Function) instead.
Null children must be filtered out because successor iterables may not contain nulls: Usage Examples: Note: the successor function must not return `null`; return an empty Iterable for leaf nodes.
The function itself is first invoked when a traversal method is called (once per start node, see the class note), so an exception it throws for a start node propagates from that call.
methods.performance: While traversing, the traverser will use O(H) space (where H is the number of nodes that have been seen but not yet visited, that is, the "horizon").
examples:
a     b      c
  / \   / \     |
 /   \ /   \    |
d     e     f   g
      |

methods.javadoc_summary: Assigns a "bucket" index in the range `[0, buckets)` to the given hash code using consistent hashing.
methods.returns: a bucket index in the range `[0, buckets)`
contract: Specifically, `consistentHash(h, n)` equals: `n - 1`, with approximate probability `1/n` `consistentHash(h, n - 1)`, otherwise (probability `1 - 1/n`) This property makes consistent hashing ideal for distributed systems where you want to minimize redistribution when adding or removing nodes.
When the number of buckets increases from n-1 to n, only approximately 1/n of the items need to be remapped.

methods.javadoc_summary: Extracts the request body and MIME type from a HAR request entry.
methods.returns: a tuple where the first element is the request body text (may be `null` if the request has no body) and the second element is the MIME type (may be `null` if no MIME type is present).

methods.javadoc_summary: Converts a header value to its string representation.
methods.returns: the string representation of the header value, or an empty string if `headerValue` is `null`
contract: An array is not a `Collection` and is rendered by `N.stringOf` as a JSON array literal - `new String[] {"a", "b"}` becomes `["a", "b"]`, which is what would go on the wire - so pass a `Collection` (for example `Arrays.asList(array)`) when a comma-joined value is intended.

Not every multiply-valued header field is comma-separated: use #valueOf(String, Object) when the header name is known, so that a field with its own list grammar (such as `Cookie`) is rendered with the separator its grammar requires.
examples:

methods.javadoc_summary: Sets a header only if it is not already present, following Map#putIfAbsent semantics.
methods.returns: This HttpHeaders instance for method chaining
contract: The header is set when there is currently no mapping for the given name or when the name is explicitly mapped to `null`; in both cases such a name is treated as absent and the new value is stored.
If the name is already mapped to a non-`null` value, this method does nothing and that existing value is preserved.
examples:
headers.setIfAbsent("User-Agent", "MyApp/1.0");   // set: no existing mapping
headers.set("X-Trace", (Object) null);
headers.setIfAbsent("X-Trace", "abc");           // set: previous value was null (treated as absent)
headers.setIfAbsent("User-Agent", "Other/2.0");  // no-op: already mapped to a non-null value

types.name: HttpResponse
types.javadoc_summary: Represents an immutable HTTP response containing status code, headers, and body.

methods.name: isSuccessful
methods.signature: public boolean isSuccessful()
methods.javadoc_summary: Checks if the response status code indicates success.
methods.returns: `true` if the response indicates success, `false` otherwise
contract: Returns `true` if the status code is in the range `[200, 300)`, which means the request was successfully received, understood, and accepted.

methods.name: requestUrl
methods.signature: public String requestUrl()
methods.javadoc_summary: Gets the URL of the original request that generated this response.
methods.returns: The request URL as a string
examples:
HttpResponse response = client.get(HttpResponse.class);
String url = response.requestUrl();  // e.g. "http://localhost:18080/users"

methods.name: requestSentAtMillis
methods.signature: public long requestSentAtMillis()
methods.javadoc_summary: Gets the timestamp when the request was sent, in milliseconds since epoch.
methods.returns: The request sent timestamp in milliseconds

methods.name: responseReceivedAtMillis
methods.signature: public long responseReceivedAtMillis()
methods.javadoc_summary: Gets the timestamp when the response was received, in milliseconds since epoch.
methods.returns: The response received timestamp in milliseconds

methods.name: statusCode
methods.signature: public int statusCode()
methods.javadoc_summary: Gets the HTTP status code of the response.
methods.returns: The HTTP status code

methods.name: message
methods.signature: public String message()
methods.javadoc_summary: Gets the status message associated with the status code.
methods.returns: The status message
examples:
HttpResponse response = client.get(HttpResponse.class);
String message = response.message();  // e.g. "OK" for status 200, "Not Found" for 404

methods.name: headers
methods.signature: public Map<String, List<String>> headers()
methods.javadoc_summary: Gets all response headers as a map.
methods.returns: an unmodifiable map of header names to their values; an empty unmodifiable map if no headers were received (never `null`)
examples:
Map<String, List<String>> headers = response.headers();
List<String> contentType = headers.get("Content-Type");   // null if the server sent "content-type"

methods.name: body
methods.signature: public byte[] body()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns a copy of the raw response body as a byte array.
methods.returns: a copy of the response body as a byte array; an empty array if no body was received (never `null`)

methods.returns: the deserialized response body, or `null` if `resultClass` is `Void.class`. A successful response without content (a HEAD request, or a 204 or 205 status) is not mapped to `null`: it is decoded from empty input, so `String.class` yields `""` and `byte[].class` an empty array. A 304 status is not 2xx, so it throws HttpResponseException like any other non-2xx status. If `resultClass` is `Response.class`, the caller must close the returned response.
examples:
User user = OkHttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/users/123")
    .execute(HttpMethod.GET, User.class);

methods.javadoc_summary: Converts a cURL command string into Java code for creating an HttpRequest.
methods.returns: Java code string for creating an equivalent HttpRequest, formatted with proper indentation and line separators
contract: HTTP Method Detection: If `-X` is specified, uses that method If `-d` is present without `-X`, defaults to POST If `-I` (or `--head`) is present without `-X`, defaults to HEAD Otherwise defaults to GET `PATCH` and `CONNECT` are emitted as `.execute(HttpMethod.PATCH)` / `.execute(HttpMethod.CONNECT)`, which HttpRequest rejects at run time with an UnsupportedOperationException because `java.net.HttpURLConnection` cannot issue them.

If a request body is present and the resolved method accepts one, it is declared as a separate `requestBody` variable for readability; otherwise the body is omitted and the generated code carries a comment saying so.
Attached data defaults to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` when no Content-Type header was supplied, matching cURL's data options.
Empty contributions are ignored when combining.

methods.javadoc_summary: Builds a cURL command string from HTTP request parameters.
methods.returns: a formatted cURL command string with line separators, ready for execution
contract: It handles proper quoting and escaping of all components to ensure the command works correctly when executed.

The generated cURL command includes: HTTP method using the `-X` flag (`-I` for HEAD, which is what curl requires - unless a body is given, since curl refuses `-I` together with a data option; then `-X HEAD` is used) URL enclosed in the specified quote character, with `--globoff` to preserve literal brackets and braces All headers using `-H` flags with proper quoting and escaping; a header whose value resolves to an empty or all-whitespace string is written as `-H 'Name;'`, curl's spelling for "send this header empty" (`-H 'Name: '` would instead tell curl to remove the header, because curl skips the whitespace after the colon) Request body using `--data-raw` if body is not empty; a leading `@` is sent literally Content-Type header if body is present, `headers` carries no `Content-Type` entry at all - one present with a `null`, empty or blank value counts as present, so a command never carries two `Content-Type` lines - and `bodyContentType` is not blank (a blank one could only be written as `-H 'Content-Type: '`, which removes the header) Special handling: If `body` is not empty but Content-Type header is not present in `headers`, and `bodyContentType` is not blank, the Content-Type header is automatically added Header values are converted using the field-aware HttpHeaders#valueOf(String, Object), including its handling of java.util.Collection (joined with `", "`, or with `"; "` on the `Cookie` field) and java.util.Date/java.time.Instant (HTTP-date formatted) values URLs, header names and values, and bodies are escaped for the chosen `quoteChar`: inside single quotes each `'` becomes `'\''`; inside double quotes `\ " $ `` are backslash-escaped The command is formatted with line separators at the beginning and end A command that sends a body with an explicitly empty `Content-Type` (`-H 'Content-Type;'`) converts back to Java code only through #curlToOkHttpRequestCode(String): #curlToHttpRequestCode(String) rejects it because `HttpRequest` replaces an empty body Content-Type with a default, so the generated code would send a different request.

methods.javadoc_summary: Sets the Content-Type header based on the request body type if not already present.

methods.javadoc_summary: Sets a custom handler for processing collection property values during deserialization.

methods.name: isWriteNullToEmpty

methods.javadoc_summary: Checks if `null` bean properties should be written as empty values.
methods.returns: `true` if `null` CharSequence/collection/array/Map bean properties should be written as `""`/`[]`/{}, `false` otherwise

methods.name: setWriteNullToEmpty
methods.signature: public JsonSerConfig setWriteNullToEmpty(final boolean writeNullToEmpty)

params.name: writeNullToEmpty
params.javadoc: `true` to write surviving `null` CharSequence/collection/array/Map bean properties as `""`/`[]`/{}, `false` to write them as `null`

methods.javadoc_summary: Sets whether `null` bean properties should be written as empty values during serialization.
methods.returns: `this` instance for method chaining
contract: Only bean properties are affected, and only when they survive the exclusion strategy: the default exclusion (Exclusion#NULL, applied when no exclusion is set on the config or on the bean's `@JsonXmlConfig`) drops `null` properties before this flag is consulted, so the flag has no visible effect unless the effective exclusion is Exclusion#NONE, selected through #setExclusion(Exclusion) or the bean annotation.

This flag only wins over #setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(boolean), for the slots that have an empty form: a surviving `null` `CharSequence`/collection/array/`Map` property is emptied even when that flag is off.
A `null` number or boolean has no empty form, so #setWriteNullNumberAsZero(boolean) / #setWriteNullBooleanAsFalse(boolean) still apply to such a property when they are on, writing `0` / `false`.

methods.javadoc_summary: Registers a class with this parser instance for improved performance.

A parser-local registration uses the default serializer even when the same class has a global custom serializer.

A global or built-in registration ID is retained; otherwise the class receives the next free ID when it is applied (after the built-in types, all global registrations and this parser's earlier `register(Class)` calls; see the class documentation), so the ID is guaranteed to be the same in another JVM only if that JVM makes the same registration calls in the same order with the same library version.

params.javadoc: the class to register (must not be `null`)

methods.javadoc_summary: Registers a class with Kryo for serialization.
contract: If this class was registered previously through another overload, this call replaces that registration; the most recent call is authoritative.

Any other class receives the next free ID when it is applied: every Kryo instance applies the built-in types, then the global registrations kind by kind - `registerKryo(Class)`, then `registerKryo(Class, int)`, then `registerKryo(Class, Serializer)`, then `registerKryo(Class, Serializer, int)` - each kind in the order of its calls (a class registered again takes the position of its latest call), then the registrations of its own parser in the same way (see the KryoParser class documentation).
Two JVMs are therefore guaranteed to assign the same ID to such a class only when they make the same registration calls in the same order with the same library version.

params.javadoc: the configuration supplying the string quotation; must not be `null`

methods.javadoc_summary: Tells whether `str`, the text a type handler wrote for a value, is already enclosed in quotes, so that a map-key writer can emit it as-is instead of wrapping it in another pair of quotes.
methods.returns: `true` if `str` starts and ends with the same quote character, being a double quote or the configured string quotation; `false` otherwise
contract: The text counts as quoted if it is at least two characters long, its first character is either a double quote (`"`) or the non-zero string quotation of `config` (for example `'`), and its last character is the same as its first.
examples:
JsonSerConfig config = JsonSerConfig.create();                          // stringQuotation = '"'
ParserUtil.isQuoted("\"5\"", config);                                   // returns true
ParserUtil.isQuoted("'5'", config);                                     // returns false
ParserUtil.isQuoted("5", config);                                       // returns false
ParserUtil.isQuoted("\"", config);                                      // returns false

JsonSerConfig singleQuoted = JsonSerConfig.create().setStringQuotation('\'');
ParserUtil.isQuoted("'5'", singleQuoted);                               // returns true
ParserUtil.isQuoted("\"5\"", singleQuoted);                             // returns true
ParserUtil.isQuoted("'5\"", singleQuoted);                              // returns false

A `null` input returns `null` in the number-format branch and most date-format readers; without formatting it follows the property type's `valueOf` policy (primitive types return their default value). params.name: excelFile
params.javadoc: the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file.

throws.condition: if `excelFile` is `null`, or the workbook has no sheet at index 0, or the header row contains duplicate non-empty column names (whitespace-only names count as non-empty), or `excelFile` is empty (zero bytes), an OLE2 document that is not a workbook (such as a Word file), an Excel 5.0/95 workbook or data that starts like a ZIP entry but holds no readable one (see the class-level note on unreadable sources).
if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating its workbook, or closing the workbook fails with an `IOException`

methods.javadoc_summary: Loads the first sheet from the specified Excel file into a Dataset.
methods.returns: a Dataset containing the sheet data with the first row as column names, or an empty Dataset if the sheet is empty.
contract: Header handling: the `readDatasetFromSheet` family always consumes the first physically defined row returned by the sheet iterator as the header row and uses the #CELL_TO_STRING rendering of those cells as column names (a numeric header `2024` becomes `"2024.0"`, a formula its text); only a missing cell, a `CellType.BLANK` cell or an empty string is replaced by a synthesized unique `"Column_i"` (with a numeric suffix when needed), while a whitespace-only name is kept as-is and may not repeat.

fields.name: CELL_GETTER
fields.value: (cell)->switch (cell.getCellType()) { case STRING -> yield cell.getStringCellValue(); case NUMERIC -> yield cell.getNumericCellValue(); case BOOLEAN -> yield cell.getBooleanCellValue(); case FORMULA -> yield cell.getCellFormula(); case BLANK -> yield ""; case ERROR -> yield ""; default -> throw new RuntimeException("Unsupported cell type: " + cell.getCellType()); }

fields.name: CELL_TO_STRING
fields.value: (cell)->switch (cell.getCellType()) { case STRING -> yield cell.getStringCellValue(); case NUMERIC -> yield String.valueOf(cell.getNumericCellValue()); case BOOLEAN -> yield String.valueOf(cell.getBooleanCellValue()); case FORMULA -> yield cell.getCellFormula(); case BLANK -> yield ""; case ERROR -> yield ""; default -> throw new RuntimeException("Unsupported cell type: " + cell.getCellType()); }

methods.javadoc_summary: Associates the specified element with the specified key in this pool.
methods.returns: `true` if the mapping was successfully added, `false` otherwise
contract: If the pool previously contained a mapping for the key, the old element is detached and accounted with Caller#REMOVE_REPLACE_CLEAR before the new value is inserted.
Detachment still happens when the later insertion fails (capacity/memory rejection), so a failing `put` can remove the previous mapping for `key`.

The old element is not destroyed when it is the same instance as `value` (re-pooling the same instance moves it to the newest insertion position on success; a failed re-pooling retains its original insertion position and memory charge).

The put operation returns `false` (does not insert) if: The element has already expired (on entry, or by the time it is checked under the lock) The pool is at capacity and either auto-balancing is disabled, or balancing did not free a slot The element would exceed memory constraints (when a memory measure is configured) and balancing did not free enough memory The memory measure returns a negative size or throws an exception A value that the memory rule must reject whatever balancing frees (its measure is negative or failed, or it is larger than `maxMemorySize` on its own) is rejected without auto-balancing other entries; a previous mapping for `key` is still detached as described above.

methods.javadoc_summary: Attempts to associate the specified element with the specified key, waiting if necessary for a capacity slot to become available.
methods.returns: `true` if the value was successfully added, `false` if the timeout elapsed (or the value was already/became expired, or memory constraints rejected it)
contract: This is the keyed mirror of ObjectPool#add(Poolable, long, TimeUnit): when the pool is at capacity and auto-balancing is disabled, this method blocks until a slot frees up (because another thread removes/evicts an entry), the timeout expires, or the thread is interrupted.
Rejection of one waiting candidate allows other waiting candidates to proceed when space is available.

When auto-balancing is enabled (the PoolFactory default), a full pool is first balanced under the lock - a balance-factor share of the existing mappings is detached and destroyed with Poolable.Caller#VACATE - and the value is inserted without waiting.
Waiting for a slot occurs only when auto-balancing is disabled (or the capacity is `0`).

All other `put` semantics of #put(Object, Poolable) still apply: the previous mapping for `key` (if any, and a different instance) is removed and destroyed before insertion, an already-expired value is rejected (`false`), and a configured memory measure is consulted.
The method returns `false` if the timeout elapses before a slot becomes available.
If another thread inserts this key while the call waits, that mapping can be replaced even when the pool is full.

contract: Appends the literal `"null"` string if `x` is `null`.
implementation_notes: This method appends a string representation of `x` to `appendable` (the literal `"null"` for a `null` value). Conceptually this is the human-readable form produced by `toString()`, not the value returned by `stringOf`, which is a formatted, serializable representation (typically a JSON string) that #valueOf(String) can convert back into an equivalent value. For values whose nested structure makes the two forms differ (collections, maps, arrays), `appendTo` emits the unquoted, `toString()`-style form; it is therefore not, in the general contract, a plain `appendable.append(x == null? NULL_STRING: stringOf(x))`. (For value types whose human-readable and serialized forms coincide, the appended text is naturally identical to `stringOf(x)`.)

implementation_notes: This method appends a string representation of `x` to `appendable` (the literal `"null"` for a `null` value). Conceptually this is the human-readable form produced by `toString()`, not the value returned by `stringOf`, which is a formatted, serializable representation (typically a JSON string) that #valueOf(String) can convert back into an equivalent value. For values whose nested structure makes the two forms differ (collections, maps, arrays), `appendTo` emits the unquoted, `toString()`-style form; it is therefore not, in the general contract, a plain `appendable.append(x == null? NULL_STRING: stringOf(x))`. (For value types whose human-readable and serialized forms coincide, the appended text is naturally identical to `stringOf(x)`.)

methods.javadoc_summary: Appends the `toString()`-style string representation of an object array to an Appendable.
contract: Optimizes performance by using buffered writers when appropriate.

When that declared type is `Object` the handler of the element's runtime class is used instead, exactly as `AbstractTupleType.appendElement` - the slot writer the Pair/Triple/Tuple, `Map.Entry` and optional handlers use - resolves a slot: `ObjectType` has no `appendTo` of its own, so it would otherwise fall back to `stringOf`, i.e.
A map, collection or bean element therefore keeps the `toString()`-style form (`[{k:1}]`, not `[{"k": 1}]`), matching what the same value appends as when it is not in a container.
implementation_notes: This method appends a string representation of `x` to `appendable` (the literal `"null"` for a `null` value). Conceptually this is the human-readable form produced by `toString()`, not the value returned by `stringOf`, which is a formatted, serializable representation (typically a JSON string) that #valueOf(String) can convert back into an equivalent value. For values whose nested structure makes the two forms differ (collections, maps, arrays), `appendTo` emits the unquoted, `toString()`-style form; it is therefore not, in the general contract, a plain `appendable.append(x == null? NULL_STRING: stringOf(x))`. (For value types whose human-readable and serialized forms coincide, the appended text is naturally identical to `stringOf(x)`.)

methods.javadoc_summary: Writes the JSON character representation of an object array to a CharacterWriter.
contract: When the element type is serializable (for example `String[]`, `Integer[]`, enum arrays) each element is written by its own type handler.

When it is not (for example `Object[]`, `Bean[]`, `Map[]`, `Object[][]`) the array is rendered the same way #stringOf(Object[]) renders it: under a com.landawn.abacus.parser.JsonSerConfig the JSON parser writes real JSON (a number stays a number, a bean becomes an object, so `new Object[] {1, "a", null, bean}` becomes `[1, "a", null, {"name": "z", "age": 3}]`), and under an XML configuration the JSON text of the array is written as escaped character content, retaining XML's rejection of present-null `Nullable` values at any nested depth.

methods.javadoc_summary: Appends the content of a Reader to the given Appendable.
contract: If the Appendable is a Writer, the content is copied directly.
In the non-Writer path, reading stops at end of stream or if a read and its retry both return zero.
implementation_notes: This method appends a string representation of `x` to `appendable` (the literal `"null"` for a `null` value). Conceptually this is the human-readable form produced by `toString()`, not the value returned by `stringOf`, which is a formatted, serializable representation (typically a JSON string) that #valueOf(String) can convert back into an equivalent value. For values whose nested structure makes the two forms differ (collections, maps, arrays), `appendTo` emits the unquoted, `toString()`-style form; it is therefore not, in the general contract, a plain `appendable.append(x == null? NULL_STRING: stringOf(x))`. (For value types whose human-readable and serialized forms coincide, the appended text is naturally identical to `stringOf(x)`.)

methods.javadoc_summary: Appends the string representation of a Triple object to the given Appendable.
contract: When that declared type is `Object` the handler of the element's runtime class is used instead, exactly as #serializeTo(CharacterWriter, Triple, JsonXmlSerConfig) does, so a map, collection or bean element keeps the `toString()`-style form rather than falling back to `ObjectType`'s JSON `stringOf`.
implementation_notes: This method appends a string representation of `x` to `appendable` (the literal `"null"` for a `null` value). Conceptually this is the human-readable form produced by `toString()`, not the value returned by `stringOf`, which is a formatted, serializable representation (typically a JSON string) that #valueOf(String) can convert back into an equivalent value. For values whose nested structure makes the two forms differ (collections, maps, arrays), `appendTo` emits the unquoted, `toString()`-style form; it is therefore not, in the general contract, a plain `appendable.append(x == null? NULL_STRING: stringOf(x))`. (For value types whose human-readable and serialized forms coincide, the appended text is naturally identical to `stringOf(x)`.)

methods.javadoc_summary: Writes the character representation of a Triple object to the given CharacterWriter.
contract: When the declared element type is `Object` the handler of the element's runtime class is used instead, so an `Object` slot holding `1` is written as `1` rather than `"1"`.

An element whose (declared or runtime) handler is not serializable - a bean, a map, a `List<Object>` - is written as embedded JSON (not as a quoted JSON string) when `config` is a `JsonSerConfig`; under any other config its `stringOf` text is written with the writer's character escaping.

methods.name: name
methods.signature: String name()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the canonical name of this type.
methods.returns: the type name
contract: The package prefixes `java.lang`, `java.util`, `java.time` and `com.landawn.abacus` are omitted when the simple name resolves back to the same class (`"String"`, `"UUID"`, `"Year"`, but `"java.util.BitSet"`, and `"com.landawn.abacus.util.function.Runnable"` because `"Runnable"` is `java.lang.Runnable`); every other class keeps its canonical (fully qualified) name, except that a non-public implementation class in those packages is shortened whenever its simple name resolves to some class (the list class of `Arrays.asList` is `"ArrayList<Object>"`).
examples:
Type.ofList(String.class).name();                    // "List<String>"
Type.of("java.util.List<java.lang.String>").name();  // "List<String>"
Type.of("ArrayList<String>").name();                 // "ArrayList<String>"

methods.name: getType
methods.signature: @SuppressWarnings({ "rawtypes", "unchecked" }) public static <T> Type<T> getType(final Class<?> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: targetClass
params.javadoc: the Class object for which to retrieve the Type

throws.condition: if `targetClass` is `null`, or if the handler selected for `targetClass` rejects its metadata (for example, duplicate enum JSON/XML names or `@JsonValue` values, or incomplete, duplicate or invalid JSON value/creator annotations).

methods.javadoc_summary: Retrieves the Type object corresponding to the specified Class object.
methods.returns: the Type object corresponding to the specified class (never `null`)
contract: If the type is not found in the cache, it creates a new Type instance and atomically publishes it for future use.
If a custom registration or another lookup publishes a mapping concurrently, that existing mapping wins and is returned.
Implementations of java.sql.Array, java.sql.Ref, java.sql.RowId, java.sql.SQLXML, and java.sql.Struct use their dedicated JDBC handlers, even when their accessors resemble bean properties.

methods.name: getType
methods.signature: @SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") public static <T> Type<T> getType(final java.lang.reflect.Type javaType) throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: javaType
params.javadoc: the java.lang.reflect.Type to convert, including Class, ParameterizedType and GenericArrayType

throws.condition: if `javaType` is `null`, if the type name format is structurally invalid, or if the handler selected for the type (or one of its type arguments) rejects its metadata (for example, incompatible value/creator annotations).

methods.javadoc_summary: Retrieves the Type object corresponding to the specified java.lang.reflect.Type.
methods.returns: the corresponding Type object (never `null`)
contract: Cache publication is atomic: when another lookup has already published a result for the same reflection type, that result is retained and returned.

methods.name: getType
methods.signature: public static <T> Type<T> getType(final String typeName) throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: typeName
params.javadoc: the name of the type to retrieve, with optional type parameters; must not be `null`, empty or blank; surrounding whitespace is ignored

throws.condition: if `typeName` is `null`, empty or blank, if the type name format is structurally invalid (a mismatched type-parameter count, unused constructor arguments on a resolved class, misplaced brackets), or if the handler selected for the type (or one of its type arguments) rejects its metadata (for example, incompatible value/creator annotations).

methods.javadoc_summary: Retrieves the Type object corresponding to the specified type name string.
methods.returns: the Type object corresponding to the type name (never `null`; an ObjectType is returned for unresolvable names)
contract: If the type pool size reaches multiples of 100, a warning is logged about the pool size.
examples:
Type<String> t1 = TypeFactory.getType("String");
t1.javaType();                  // returns String.class

Type<List<String>> t2 = TypeFactory.getType("List<String>");
t2.name();           // returns "List<String>"
t2.declaringName();  // returns "List<String>"
t2.javaType();       // returns List.class

Type<?> t3 = TypeFactory.getType("CompletelyUnknownName");
t3.isObject();                        // returns true (ObjectType fallback, not an exception)

boolean sameInstance = TypeFactory.getType(" Integer ") == TypeFactory.getType("Integer");  // true
TypeFactory.getType("List<? extends Person>").elementType().javaType();                     // Person.class

TypeFactory.getType((String) null);  // throws IllegalArgumentException
TypeFactory.getType("");             // throws IllegalArgumentException
TypeFactory.getType("String(MD5)");  // throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: typeName

methods.javadoc_summary: Returns a type already present in the type registry without attempting to load or derive a class from the supplied name.
methods.returns: the built-in, registered or previously resolved type published under exactly `typeName`, or `null` when `typeName` is `null` or empty, or when nothing has been published under that exact name
contract: This non-creating lookup is useful when a name comes from an untrusted source and class loading must not be triggered as a side effect.

methods.name: registerType
methods.signature: public static <T> void registerType(final Class<T> targetClass, final BiFunction<? super T, JsonParser, String> toStringFunction, final BiFunction<? super String, JsonParser, T> fromStringFunction) throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: targetClass
params.javadoc: the class for which to register the custom type

params.name: toStringFunction
params.javadoc: the function to convert an object of type T to a String, receives the object and a JsonParser

params.name: fromStringFunction
params.javadoc: the function to convert a String to an object of type T, receives the string and a JsonParser

throws.condition: if `targetClass`, `toStringFunction`, or `fromStringFunction` is `null`, if `targetClass` has a built-in type, if a type has already been resolved and cached for it by a prior lookup by class (`getType(Class)`, bean introspection, serialization), or if a type is already registered under the new type's name (as returned by Type#name()). The new type is named after the canonical class name, shortened to the simple name as Type#name() describes (for a public class in `java.lang`, `java.util`, `java.time` or `com.landawn.abacus` only when that simple name resolves to the same class, e.g. `"Year"` for `java.time.Year`), so a fallback that an earlier lookup by that name (`getType("com.example.Foo")`, `getType("Year")`) cached also makes this method throw; to supersede such a fallback, use #registerType(Class, Type) with a differently named type or #registerType(String, Class, BiFunction, BiFunction).

methods.javadoc_summary: Registers a custom Type for the specified target class with custom serialization/deserialization functions.
contract: This method allows you to define how objects of a specific class should be converted to and from strings.

The new type is named after the canonical class name, shortened to the simple name as Type#name() describes (for a public class in `java.lang`, `java.util`, `java.time` or `com.landawn.abacus` only when that simple name resolves to the same class, e.g. `"Year"` for `java.time.Year`), so a fallback that an earlier lookup by that name (`getType("com.example.Foo")`, `getType("Year")`) cached also makes this method throw; to supersede such a fallback, use #registerType(Class, Type) with a differently named type or #registerType(String, Class, Function, Function).

methods.javadoc_summary: Appends the string representation of a ZonedDateTime to an Appendable.
contract: If the ZonedDateTime is `null`, it appends the string `"null"`.

serializeTo: `appendTo` produces a plain, `toString()`-style rendering with no JSON/XML quoting or escaping (for general text output), whereas `serializeTo` writes the configured JSON/XML serialized form, including string quotation for non-LONG date/time formats when requested by config.
implementation_notes: This method appends a string representation of `x` to `appendable` (the literal `"null"` for a `null` value). Conceptually this is the human-readable form produced by `toString()`, not the value returned by `stringOf`, which is a formatted, serializable representation (typically a JSON string) that #valueOf(String) can convert back into an equivalent value. For values whose nested structure makes the two forms differ (collections, maps, arrays), `appendTo` emits the unquoted, `toString()`-style form; it is therefore not, in the general contract, a plain `appendable.append(x == null? NULL_STRING: stringOf(x))`. (For value types whose human-readable and serialized forms coincide, the appended text is naturally identical to `stringOf(x)`.)

type.appendTo(sb, ZonedDateTime.now());   // Appends formatted date/time

params.name: servers
params.javadoc: the string containing server addresses to parse; must not be `null` or empty

throws.condition: if the servers string is `null` or empty, contains no address after splitting and trimming, or contains invalid addresses (missing colon, an unbracketed multi-colon address that is itself a valid IPv6 literal or whose host part is not one, invalid port number, empty host or port, or port out of valid range 0-65535).

methods.javadoc_summary: Parses a string containing whitespace or comma separated host or IP addresses and port numbers into a List of InetSocketAddress instances.
methods.returns: a non-empty list of InetSocketAddress instances corresponding to the parsed addresses
contract: An unbracketed address holding more than one colon is split only when that reading is the only possible one: if the whole token is itself a valid IPv6 literal it is rejected as ambiguous (`"fe80::1:8080"`, `"::1:1121"`), and otherwise the part before the last colon must itself be a valid IPv6 literal (`"::1:11211"` is accepted, `"abc:def:1234"` is not).

This method supports various address formats including: Standard format: `"host:port host2:port"` or `"host:port, host2:port"` IPv4 addresses: `"192.168.1.1:8080"` IPv6, bracketed: `"[::1]:11211"`, `"[fe80::1]:8080"` IPv6, unbracketed and unambiguous: `"::1:11211"` (but `"::1:1121"` is rejected - it is itself a valid address) Hostnames: `"localhost:8080"` or `"example.com:443"` The port number must be a valid integer in the range 0-65535.
Each address must contain at least one colon separating the host and port.
Both the host part and port part must be non-empty.
That call may block on DNS, and a host that cannot be resolved yields an unresolved address rather than an exception - test InetSocketAddress#isUnresolved() if that matters to the caller.

methods.name: getAddressList
methods.signature: public static List<InetSocketAddress> getAddressList(final Collection<String> servers) throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: servers
params.javadoc: a collection of server addresses where each string is in the format `"host:port"`; must not be `null`

throws.condition: if `servers` is `null` or empty, contains a `null` element, or any server address is invalid (missing colon, an unbracketed multi-colon address that is itself a valid IPv6 literal or whose host part is not one, invalid port number, empty host or port, or port out of valid range 0-65535).

methods.javadoc_summary: Converts a collection of server address strings into a list of InetSocketAddress instances.
methods.returns: a non-empty list of InetSocketAddress instances corresponding to the server addresses
contract: Each string in the collection should be in the format `"host:port"`.

This method parses each address string individually by finding the last colon to separate the host from the port; an unbracketed address holding more than one colon is split only when that reading is the only possible one, exactly as in #getAddressList(String).

Supported address formats: Hostnames: `"localhost:8080"`, `"example.com:443"` IPv4 addresses: `"192.168.1.1:8080"` IPv6, bracketed: `"[::1]:11211"`, `"[fe80::1]:8080"` IPv6, unbracketed and unambiguous: `"::1:11211"` Each address must contain at least one colon separating the host and port.
The port must be a valid integer in the range 0-65535.
Both host and port parts must be non-empty.
That call may block on DNS, and a host that cannot be resolved yields an unresolved address rather than an exception - test InetSocketAddress#isUnresolved() if that matters to the caller.
examples:
List<String> serverStrings = Arrays.asList("127.0.0.1:8080", "192.168.1.1:8080");
List<InetSocketAddress> addresses = AddrUtil.getAddressList(serverStrings);

methods.javadoc_summary: Creates an InetSocketAddress from a URL object by extracting its host and port information.

If neither an explicit nor a default port is available (i.e., the resolved port is outside the valid range 0-65535), an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.

methods.javadoc_summary: Generates a new array of a specified length, with all elements set to the element value.

methods.javadoc_summary: Concatenates two two-dimensional boolean arrays element-wise by combining their corresponding row elements.
methods.returns: a new two-dimensional boolean array containing the element-wise concatenation of the input arrays. The length equals max(a.length, b.length). Each row in the result is the concatenation of the corresponding rows from `a` and `b`.

params.name: b

if a copied element, row, or layer is incompatible with the runtime component type selected from the corresponding non-null input arrays.

methods.javadoc_summary: Concatenates two two-dimensional arrays of generic type T element-wise by combining their corresponding row elements.
methods.returns: a new two-dimensional array containing the element-wise concatenation of the input arrays. The length equals max(a.length, b.length). Each row in the result is the concatenation of the corresponding rows from `a` and `b`. Returns `null` only when both `a` and `b` are `null`.
contract: For each row index: If both arrays have a row at that index, the rows are concatenated together If only one array has a row at that index, a copy of that row is used in the result If neither array has a row at that index (both are null), the result row is `null` Deliberate divergence from the primitive overloads.

This method propagates `null` instead, consistently on every path, so that a result row is `null` exactly when both input rows are `null` - matching N#concat(Object[], Object[]), which returns `null` for two `null` rows, and matching the top-level rule that `concat2D(null, null)` is `null` rather than an empty array.
Result component type: the returned array's runtime component type is always `a`'s, whatever `a`'s length - it falls back to `b`'s only when `a` itself is `null`.
